method: Independent read-only source audit of the exact 23 assigned test files. Read every actual test/fixture body and assertion in bounded text batches (including all parameterized cases), rather than using AST, file names or hashes as a source-coverage surrogate. Reviewed asynchronous promise resolution/rejection, effect and listener ownership, cleanup, storage/global-mock/fake-timer isolation, duplicate submission and unknown-receipt behavior, explicit consent, identity checks, resource limits, and behavioral adequacy. Traced applicable assertions into current production component/helper bodies and their actual App -> Workspace -> Settings/ExtensionsPanel or WorkspacePanel parent paths, including parent keys, retained hidden panels and read-versus-owner epochs. Checked current Vitest configuration and package configuration for execution isolation context. No previous checkout, history, prior audit report or findings were consulted. The formal frozen pass started at the recorded before-integrity timestamp; early reconnaissance tests were read again within that bracket. Used the pinned Node v24.22.1 executable to recompute all 1,901 raw SHA-256 hashes and call the exported canonical snapshot(process.cwd(), true) from scripts/snapshot.mjs before and after the source pass; compared inventory names, count and digest in both directions. All 23 assigned files completed; no actionable issue was identified. This is source-review evidence, not a claim of executed test success or full production coverage.
limitations: No test suite, targeted test, build, typecheck or browser execution was run in this supplemental source-only review. The user gate remains two complete clean rounds; this report does not itself authorize full tests.

No native Codex process, external MCP/provider/network integration, microphone/WebRTC browser device, deployment, or remote operation was exercised; these behaviors were assessed from the assigned local fixture tests and current reachable production source.
Production files were cross-referenced for the assigned test contracts and actual parent reachability; independent full production-file review remains the separate production audit scope.
